rv.q: This is, unashamedly, a Mark Rylance star vehicle and it's hard to imagine another actor providing a similar focal point for a drama that slightly loses its bearings in the second half.

It’s almost a theatrical rebuff but it draws us into a borderline psychological state twixt sleep and wake, lucidity and incomprehension, jest and earnest that has us – like Philippe’s exasperated adherents – hanging on every word.

Rylance arming and saddling up on a wooden horse is a glorious and painterly baroque climax. Farinelli descending from the skies scattering gold petals is a nod to the theatre of Monteverdi and Cavalli.

cn.t: Rylance delivers a magnificent star turn that captivates throughout, though the drama loses some focus in its second half. Critics praise the lead performance while noting structural unevenness.
